builder_plan.scenario: A support or data assistant repeats work across related customer requests.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's memory change in a replay of past tasks, with separate memory per customer.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current memory pipeline plus a no-memory control using the same agent.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, stale memories, retrieval misses, response latency, and all memory maintenance costs.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Belief-State Management Meets Rubric Rewards for Agentic Forecasting
summary: Proactive Belief-State Management replaces the standard ReAct pattern of accumulating all reasoning and evidence in one growing context by having the agent fold its context into a compact belief state and reset, while SEIPH replaces outcome-only rewards with a five-dimensional outcome-blind process rubric for RL post-training. The harness costs extra fold/restart steps and agent-loop complexity, and the full method costs PPO/GRPO training of a 35B model plus rubric reward computation, which exceeds the reader's infrastructure. Compression can discard decision-relevant evidence, the outcome-blind rubric may reward plausible-sounding but wrong reasoning, and the forecasting gains are domain-specific and may not transfer to other agentic tasks.
rationale: The belief-state fold harness can be implemented over third-party APIs and reportedly improves even untrained models, but the claimed Brier-score advantage depends on a 35B PPO/GRPO training stage that the reader cannot reproduce, so harness-level validation on their own forecasting workload is required.
technique: Belief-state context folding with rubric RL rewards

claims.statement: Proactive Belief-State Management replaces the standard ReAct pattern of accumulating all reasoning and evidence in one growing context by having the agent fold its context into a compact belief state and reset, while SEIPH replaces outcome-only rewards with a five-dimensional outcome-blind process rubric for RL post-training. The harness costs extra fold/restart steps and agent-loop complexity, and the full method costs PPO/GRPO training of a 35B model plus rubric reward computation, which exceeds the reader's infrastructure. Compression can discard decision-relevant evidence, the outcome-blind rubric may reward plausible-sounding but wrong reasoning, and the forecasting gains are domain-specific and may not transfer to other agentic tasks.

DeepForecaster-PPO (35B) achieves the best Brier score on ForecastBench and Polymarket-Sim, outperforming agents built on much larger frontier models; the PBM harness alone also improves the untrained base model. No multiplicative factor is stated.
